title: Slab Access Payment Computation for Interior Lines under Utility Line Protection Plans
content:
# Slab Access Payment Computation

Claims Finance computation note for the Bridgewell Utility Line Protection Plans (interior supply and drain lines).

## The calculation

The slab access payment is figured once per service request, on the day it is booked and from the plan's records as they stand that day; periods said to run to the request date end on the service request's request date. The slab access figure is the plan's slab access allowance as a flat amount, whatever the contractor charges for the opening. The slab access payment is never more than the interior occurrence benefit still open, which is the plan's interior plumbing occurrence cap less every amount already authorized, net of reversals, on the service request and on the earlier request whose occurrence it belongs to: for a recall reported no later than the plan's repair guarantee days after the most recent completed repair on the same line, the request of that completed repair, and for a new failure reported no more than the slab continuation days (14 days) after a temporary repair was authorized on another request for the same line, that temporary-repair request. The slab access payment is rounded to the cent once, at the end.

## Inputs and where they are read

| Input | Read from |
|---|---|
| Slab access allowance | a figure of the plan held |
| Interior plumbing occurrence cap | a figure of the plan held |
| Repair guarantee days | a figure of the plan held |
| Slab continuation days | 14 calendar days |
| Amounts already authorized and reversed | the plan's claim history, by service request |
| Request type, line and request date | the service request record |
| Most recent completed repair on the same line | completion entries in the claim history |
| Temporary repair authorized on another request for the same line | temporary-repair authorizations in the claim history |

## Which earlier request joins the service request

| Service request | Earlier request whose amounts are also deducted from the cap |
|---|---|
| a recall reported no later than the repair guarantee days after the most recent completed repair on the same line | the request of that completed repair |
| a new failure reported no more than 14 days after a temporary repair was authorized on another request for the same line | that temporary-repair request |
| any other request | none; only the service request's own amounts are deducted |

*Boundary case:* a new failure reported on the 14th day after the temporary repair was authorized on another request joins that request; one reported on the 15th day does not.

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures, not plan values)

Assume a slab access allowance of $400.00 and an interior plumbing occurrence cap of $2000.00.

1. A new-failure request with nothing yet authorized on it and no linked earlier request: the open benefit is $2000.00; the figure is $400.00; the payment is $400.00.
2. The same request with $1750.00 already authorized and $50.00 of that reversed: net amounts are $1700.00; the open benefit is $300.00; the payment is $300.00.
3. A recall within the guarantee period, with $1200.00 net on the request of the completed repair and $500.00 net on the recall itself: the open benefit is $300.00; the payment is $300.00.
4. If the amounts on the linked requests already reach the cap, the open benefit is $0.00 and the payment is $0.00.
